title: Lincoln University celebrates top academic achievements at 2026 Honors Convocation
text:
Lincoln University of Missouri recognized its highest-achieving students during the 2026 Honors Convocation held on April 23 in Mitchell Auditorium, Richardson Fine Arts Center.
The annual event highlights the academic accomplishments of students across all schools and departments, providing recognition and encouragement for their continued efforts. The ceremony is an important tradition that supports students as they work toward their educational goals at Lincoln.
President John Moseley addressed the honorees, saying, “Today, take pride in what you’ve accomplished. You’ve earned this recognition. But understand this — this is not the finish line. It is the standard. Keep raising it. Keep challenging yourselves. Keep stepping into opportunities that stretch you, test you and move you forward. Because what you are building here does not stop with you. It continues through you — in your careers, in your communities and in the lives you will impact.”
Chief Justice Natalie E. Hudson of the Minnesota Supreme Court also spoke to students during the convocation. Hudson said she remains optimistic about the future “because of universities like Lincoln and young people like yourself.” She added, “What you’ve learned here at Lincoln has more than prepared you to engage with others in this manner to have healthy debates where you listen to one another respectfully and work collaboratively to solve problems and enrich your communities,” she said. “This is your time on the world stage. This is your time to lead our country on the next leg of this journey towards a more perfect union.”
Lincoln University Cooperative Extension offers a wide range of programs including competitive Division II athletics and its Marching Musical Storm band according to its official website. The university maintains a diverse student body from across both the United States and internationally according to its official website. Students can choose from more than 50 undergraduate and master’s degree programs according to its official website. The institution emphasizes education as well as community development through these offerings according to its official website.
According to its official website, Lincoln University Cooperative Extension is unique as it was established by formerly enslaved Black soldiers—making it the only historically Black college or university founded under such circumstances according to its official website.
The celebration underscores Lincoln University’s ongoing commitment to supporting student achievement while fostering diversity within higher education.
